key_insight: Replacing Zr with Y in BCFZY cathodes yields modest proton-conductivity gains under PCFC operating gases, while low oxygen partial pressure is predicted to shift proton transport from hydroxyl to hydride species.
engineering_relevance: Cathode optimization should account for gas-dependent defect chemistry rather than assume Y doping alone will substantially improve proton conductivity.
method: Used ab initio molecular dynamics to evaluate proton tracer diffusivity in BCFZ, BCFZY0.1, and BCFY.
Modeled temperature-dependent proton concentrations using hydration, oxidation, and hydride-formation defect reactions.
Separated diffusivity and concentration contributions to proton conductivity.
evidence_signal: At 500 °C, increasing Y content from BCFZ to BCFY predicts gains of 1.7% in proton diffusivity, 3.8% in proton concentration, and 5.3% in proton conductivity under PCFC operating gas conditions.
watch_item: These simulation-based predictions are gas-condition dependent and should not be generalized to the larger experimental enhancements reported under reducing conditions.
paper_title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-δ}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells
